posts.title: Low Tide is now a book
posts.excerpt: Seven winters, eighty-four low tides and thirty-four photographs, printed in Kyoto by Hiru Press in an edition of 800.
posts.content:
Seven winters, eighty-four low tides and a little under three hundred rolls of film: Low Tide is now a book. Hiru Press has printed it in Kyoto in an edition of 800, on an uncoated stock that holds a deep black without any shine, and it will be in shops from the first of November.

The sequence is thirty-four photographs long. That number was not planned. I made the first dummy with sixty pictures, and every version after that was shorter, until the book had the length of one low tide — roughly forty minutes, if you turn the pages slowly.

Editing by taking away

My editor, Mai Kuroda, has a rule: a picture can stay only if the book is worse without it. We spread the work prints across the floor of the Kiyosumi studio and removed one at a time, for weeks. The pictures that survived are not the most dramatic ones. They are the ones that keep the silence going.

A picture can stay only if the book is worse without it.

Mai Kuroda, editor, Hiru Press

The details

  • Pages 112, Swiss-bound, 24 × 30 cm
  • Print Tritone offset on uncoated paper, Kyoto
  • Edition 800 copies; 50 with a signed 8 × 10 print

The book launches with a small show of the original prints at Gallery Hiru from 1 to 16 November. I will be there every Saturday afternoon, signing books and happily talking about tides. Letter readers can reserve a signed copy a week before anyone else.
